Upstash: Manage Upstash Redis, QStash, Workflow and Box resources and debug them from your agent through the Upstash Developer API.
By Upstash. Databases & Backend.
Listing page: https://mcp.tc/i/upstash
Install command: npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY
Access: Runs on your computer, started by your client. Needs an API key from Upstash in an environment variable.
Environment: UPSTASH_EMAIL (required), UPSTASH_API_KEY (required), UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY
Connects your agent to the Upstash Developer API so it can manage and debug Upstash resources across Redis, QStash, Workflow and Upstash Box. It can read and query your account, including Redis databases, QStash logs, schedules and Workflow logs, and it can make changes such as creating databases or deleting backups. A free Redis database can also be started without an account through the redis_database_start_free tool. It runs locally over stdio with npx. You need your Upstash account email…
History (new npm versions checked every 3 hours, tools not read): no change recorded yet. https://mcp.tc/i/upstash#history
Setup (call get_server with client=<id> for the full steps):
- Claude Code (claude-code): `claude mcp add --transport stdio upstash --env "UPSTASH_EMAIL=<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>" --env "UPSTASH_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>" --env "UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" -- npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY`
- Claude Desktop (claude-desktop): see client=claude-desktop
- Cursor (cursor): Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=upstash&%3D
- VS Code (vscode): see client=vscode
- Devin Desktop (devin): see client=devin
- Codex (codex): `codex mcp add upstash --env "UPSTASH_EMAIL=<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>" --env "UPSTASH_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>" --env "UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" -- npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY`
- Gemini CLI (gemini): `gemini mcp add -e "UPSTASH_EMAIL=<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>" -e "UPSTASH_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>" -e "UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" upstash npx -- -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY`
- Any client (json): see client=json

structuredContent.name: Upstash
structuredContent.tagline: Manage Upstash Redis, QStash, Workflow and Box resources and debug them from your agent through the Upstash Developer API.
structuredContent.description: Connects your agent to the Upstash Developer API so it can manage and debug Upstash resources across Redis, QStash, Workflow and Upstash Box. It can read and query your account, including Redis databases, QStash logs, schedules and Workflow logs, and it can make changes such as creating databases or deleting backups. A free Redis database can also be started without an account through the redis_database_start_free tool. It runs locally over stdio with npx. You need your Upstash account email and a Developer API key from the Upstash console. Readonly API keys are supported: the server then disables every tool that modifies state. An optional Box API key enables Box tools.
structuredContent.auth_note: Runs on your computer, started by your client. Needs an API key from Upstash in an environment variable.

env_vars.name: UPSTASH_EMAIL
env_vars.description: Email address of your Upstash account.

env_vars.name: UPSTASH_API_KEY
env_vars.description: Upstash Developer API key (create one at https://console.upstash.com/account/api).

env_vars.name: UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY
env_vars.description: Upstash Box API key for Box-related tools.

capabilities: Manage Upstash Redis databases and backups
Read Workflow logs and retry workflows
Start a free temporary Redis database without signup
Run in read-only mode with a readonly API key
example_prompts: List my Upstash Redis databases and show their usage stats.
Create a new Upstash Redis database in eu-west-1.
Show recent QStash logs for failed messages.
Start a free temporary Redis database for testing.

steps: Run this in a terminal, in your project folder:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio upstash --env "UPSTASH_EMAIL=<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>" --env "UPSTASH_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>" --env "UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" -- npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY
```
Start Claude Code and type `/mcp`. **upstash** should show as connected.
setup.code: claude mcp add --transport stdio upstash --env "UPSTASH_EMAIL=<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>" --env "UPSTASH_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>" --env "UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" -- npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY
setup.note: Add `--scope user` to make it available in every project. Replace the placeholders with your own values.

setup.label: Codex
setup.quick: `codex mcp add upstash --env "UPSTASH_EMAIL=<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>" --env "UPSTASH_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>" --env "UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" -- npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY`
steps:
```bash
codex mcp add upstash --env "UPSTASH_EMAIL=<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>" --env "UPSTASH_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>" --env "UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY=<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" -- npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY
```
Or edit `~/.codex/config.toml` directly:

```toml
[mcp_servers.upstash]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@upstash/mcp-server@latest", "--email", "YOUR_EMAIL", "--api-key", "YOUR_API_KEY"]
env = { UPSTASH_EMAIL = "<YOUR_UPSTASH_EMAIL>", UPSTASH_API_KEY = "<YOUR_UPSTASH_API_KEY>", UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY = "<YOUR_UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY>" }
```
